question.text: KB earned a total profit of Rs. 1,56,32,364.01 from alleged front-running trades in the Kanaiyalal Patel case. Under Section 15HA, the penalty may extend to three times the amount of profit made or Rs. 25 crore, whichever is higher. What is the MAXIMUM penalty exposure?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook page 80, the Section 15HA penalty is not less than Rs. 5 lakh and may extend to Rs. 25 crore or three times the amount of profits, whichever is higher. Three times the profit = 3 x Rs. 1,56,32,364.01 = Rs. 4,68,97,092.03 (about Rs. 4.69 crore). Since Rs. 25 crore is higher than Rs. 4.69 crore, the upper limit applicable here is Rs. 25 crore. The Trap: Option D (3x profit) ignores the 'whichever is higher' clause. Rs. 25 crore is not a minimum floor: page 80 sets the statutory minimum at Rs. 5 lakh, and page 154 shows an actual penalty of Rs. 25 lakh imposed in this case after mitigating circumstances. Note: The Rs. 25 crore figure is the statutory upper limit when three times the profit is lower; the actual penalty imposed by SEBI can be far less after considering mitigating factors.
